claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 3B shows absence of MOMBA-induced phosphorylation signals when CATPB is present.

claims.claim: Pre-addition of CATPB lowered the extent of basal detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum.
claims.source: Additionally, pre-addition of CATPB lowered the extent of basal detection of the receptor by the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 3B shows reduced basal signal with CATPB treatment.

claims.claim: At least part of the basal pSer296/pSer297 signal reflects agonist-independent, constitutive activity of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP.
claims.source: As CATPB possesses inverse agonist properties (Hudson et al., 2012b) this may indicate that at least part of the basal pSer296/pSer297 signal reflects agonist-independent, constitutive activity of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP.
claims.evidence: Inference based on the observation that the inverse agonist CATPB reduces basal phosphorylation (Figure 3B) and the known inverse agonist properties of CATPB.

claims.claim: Treatment with lambda protein phosphatase (LPP) eliminated MOMBA-induced detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by both pSer296/pSer297 and pThr306/pThr310 antisera.
claims.source: Now, MOMBA-induced detection of the receptor by both pSer296/pSer297 and pThr306/pThr310 antisera was eliminated (Figure 3B), as was most of the agonist-independent detection by pSer296/pSer297 (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 3B shows loss of signal after LPP treatment, confirming that the antisera detect phosphorylated forms.

claims.claim: The anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum was only able to identify hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP in immunocytochemistry after treatment with MOMBA.
claims.source: However, also in this setting, the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum was only able to identify the receptor after treatment with MOMBA (Figure 3C)
claims.evidence: Immunocytochemistry data in Figure 3C shows pThr306/pThr310 signal only in MOMBA-treated cells.

claims.claim: Pre-addition of CATPB prevented the effect of MOMBA on detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum in immunocytochemistry.
claims.source: and, once again, pre-addition of CATPB prevented the effect of MOMBA (Figure 3C) without affecting direct identification and imaging of the receptor via the eYFP tag.
claims.evidence: Immunocytochemistry data in Figure 3C shows absence of pThr306/pThr310 signal when CATPB is co-administered with MOMBA.

claims.claim: Identification of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum in immunocytochemistry was almost entirely dependent on exposure to MOMBA.
claims.source: In this setting identification of hFFAR2 DREADD-eYFP by the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum was almost entirely dependent on exposure to MOMBA (Figure 3D)
claims.evidence: Immunocytochemistry data in Figure 3D shows strong pSer296/pSer297 signal primarily in MOMBA-treated cells.

claims.claim: Pre-treatment with CATPB prevented MOMBA-induced detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum in immunocytochemistry.
claims.source: and this was also prevented by pre-treatment with CATPB (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: Immunocytochemistry data in Figure 3D shows absence of MOMBA-induced pSer296/pSer297 signal when CATPB is present.

claims.claim: FFAR2 is expressed in white adipose tissue.
claims.source: FFAR2 is known to be expressed in white adipose tissue and we previously used these hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice to define the role of this receptor as an anti-lipolytic regulator (Bolognini et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Statement supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: hFFAR2-DREADD-HA was detected predominantly as an approximately 45 kDa species in white adipose tissue, with lower levels of a 40 kDa form.
claims.source: Following SDS-PAGE of such immune precipitates from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice immunoblotting with an HA antibody resulted in detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA predominantly as an approximately 45 kDa species, with lower levels of a 40 kDa form (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 4A shows the molecular weight distribution of the receptor in white adipose tissue.

claims.claim: The pSer296/pSer297 antiserum detected hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in white adipose tissue without prior addition of a ligand.
claims.source: Notably, immunoblotting of such samples with the anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum also detected the same polypeptides. However, unlike the hFFAR2 C-terminal tail antiserum, although the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum did identify hFFAR2-DREADD-HA without prior addition of a ligand, pre-addition of MOMBA increased immune detection of the receptor (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 4A shows basal pSer296/pSer297 signal in vehicle-treated white adipose tissue.

claims.claim: Pre-addition of MOMBA increased immune detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA by the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum in white adipose tissue.
claims.source: pre-addition of MOMBA increased immune detection of the receptor (Figure 4A). This is consistent with the ligand promoting quantitatively greater levels of phosphorylation of these residues (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 4A and quantification in Figure 4B show increased pSer296/pSer297 signal after MOMBA treatment.

claims.claim: The anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum failed to detect immunoprecipitated hFFAR2-DREADD-HA from white adipose tissue in either the basal state or post-addition of MOMBA.
claims.source: In contrast, the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum failed to detect immunoprecipitated hFFAR2-DREADD-HA from white adipose tissue in either the basal state or post-addition of MOMBA (Figure 4A and B).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 4A and quantification in Figure 4B show no pThr306/pThr310 signal in white adipose tissue.

claims.claim: Thr306 and Thr310 are not and do not become phosphorylated in white adipose tissue.
claims.source: This indicates that these sites are not and do not become phosphorylated in this tissue.
claims.evidence: Conclusion drawn from the absence of pThr306/pThr310 signal in white adipose tissue (Figure 4A and B).

claims.claim: Clear identification of pSer296/pSer297 hFFAR2-DREADD-HA was detected in fixed adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA-expressing mice that had been pre-exposed to MOMBA.
claims.source: Immunohistochemical studies performed on fixed adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA-expressing mice that had been pre-exposed to MOMBA were consistent with the immunoblotting studies. Clear identification of pSer296/pSer297 hFFAR2-DREADD-HA was detected and the specificity of this was confirmed by the absence of staining in equivalent samples from CRE-MINUS mice (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4C shows pSer296/pSer297 staining in MOMBA-treated adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice but not CRE-MINUS mice.

claims.claim: No specific staining was observed for the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum in adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA-expressing mice.
claims.source: Once more, no specific staining was observed for the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4C shows absence of pThr306/pThr310 staining in adipose tissue.

claims.claim: Clear detection of pSer296/pSer297 immunostaining was observed in adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice without exposure to MOMBA.
claims.source: Clear detection of pSer296/pSer297 immunostaining was observed in adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice without exposure to MOMBA but once more the intensity of staining was markedly increased after MOMBA treatment (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4D shows basal pSer296/pSer297 staining in vehicle-treated adipose tissue.

claims.claim: The intensity of pSer296/pSer297 staining in adipose tissue was markedly increased after MOMBA treatment.
claims.source: Clear detection of pSer296/pSer297 immunostaining was observed in adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice without exposure to MOMBA but once more the intensity of staining was markedly increased after MOMBA treatment (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4D shows increased pSer296/pSer297 staining intensity after MOMBA treatment.

claims.claim: pSer296/pSer297 hFFAR2-DREADD-HA is present directly on adipocytes.
claims.source: and clear co-localisation of anti- pSer296/pSer297 immunostaining with that for perilipin-1 (Figure 4F) confirmed the presence of pSer296/pSer297 hFFAR2-DREADD-HA directly on adipocytes.
claims.evidence: Co-localization data in Figure 4F shows overlap of pSer296/pSer297 signal with perilipin-1, an adipocyte marker.

claims.claim: Anti-HA staining showed extensive and high-level expression of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in cells within Peyer's patches.
claims.source: Anti-HA staining showed extensive and high-level expression of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in cells within these structures (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 5A shows widespread HA staining in Peyer's patches.

claims.claim: Many of the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA-positive cells in Peyer's patches correspond to dendritic cells, monocytes, and/or macrophages.
claims.source: Co-staining for CD11c indicated many of the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA-positive cells correspond to dendritic cells, monocytes, and/or macrophages (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: Co-localization data in Figure 5B shows overlap of HA signal with CD11c, a marker for these immune cell types.

claims.claim: hFFAR2-DREADD-HA is well expressed by type-III innate lymphoid cells in Peyer's patches.
claims.source: Co-staining to detect the presence of the nuclear transcription factor RoRγt also indicated, as shown previously at the mRNA level for mouse FFAR2 (Chun et al., 2019), that hFFAR2-DREADD-HA is well expressed by type-III innate lymphoid cells (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: Co-localization data in Figure 5C shows overlap of HA signal with RoRγt, a marker for type-III innate lymphoid cells, and is supported by previous mRNA expression data.

claims.claim: hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in Peyer's patches showed a more diffuse pattern of immunostaining than observed from white adipose tissue, potentially reflecting a more complex pattern of post-translational modifications.
claims.source: Anti-HA immunoblotting of such material indicated a more diffuse pattern of immunostaining than observed from white adipose tissue (Figure 5D). This may reflect a more complex pattern of post-translational modifications, including differing extents of N-glycosylation (see later) than observed in white adipose tissue (compare Figure 5D with Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 5D shows broader molecular weight distribution compared to Figure 4A, suggesting different post-translational modifications.

claims.claim: In Peyer's patches, hFFAR2-DREADD-HA became phosphorylated on Thr306/Thr310 in a MOMBA-dependent manner, with no detection of phosphorylation of these residues without agonist treatment.
claims.source: Parallel immunoblots of such samples with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum now indicated that, in contrast to adipocytes, hFFAR2-DREADD-HA became phosphorylated on these residues in a MOMBA-dependent manner, with no detection of phosphorylation of these residues without agonist treatment (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 5D shows pThr306/pThr310 signal only after MOMBA treatment in Peyer's patches.

claims.claim: The effect of MOMBA on pThr306/pThr310 phosphorylation in Peyer's patches was clearly mediated by the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA receptor because anti-pThr306/pThr310 recognition was entirely lacking when MOMBA was added after the addition of CATPB.
claims.source: Moreover, this effect of MOMBA was clearly mediated by the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA receptor because anti-pThr306/pThr310 recognition was entirely lacking when MOMBA was added after the addition of the hFFAR2 antagonist/inverse agonist CATPB (Figure 5D and E) that blocks this receptor with high affinity (Hudson et al., 2012b; Hudson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 5D and quantification in Figure 5E show absence of pThr306/pThr310 signal when CATPB is co-administered with MOMBA.

claims.claim: Basal detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA by the anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum in Peyer's patches was low and was increased markedly by pre-treatment with MOMBA.
claims.source: Similar outcomes were obtained in this tissue with the anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum. Basal detection of the immune-captured receptor was low and this was increased markedly by pre-treatment with MOMBA (Figure 5D and E).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 5D and quantification in Figure 5E show low basal and increased MOMBA-induced pSer296/pSer297 signal in Peyer's patches.

claims.claim: The effect of MOMBA on pSer296/pSer297 phosphorylation in Peyer's patches was not observed when cells were exposed to CATPB in addition to MOMBA.
claims.source: As for the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum the effect of MOMBA on recognition of the receptor was not observed when cells were exposed to CATPB in addition to MOMBA (Figure 5D and E).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 5D and quantification in Figure 5E show absence of MOMBA-induced pSer296/pSer297 signal when CATPB is present.

claims.claim: Immunostaining of fixed Peyer's patch tissue with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum confirmed the marked agonist dependence of recognition of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in such cells.
claims.source: Immunostaining of fixed Peyer's patch tissue with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum confirmed the marked agonist dependence of recognition of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in such cells (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 5F shows pThr306/pThr310 staining primarily in MOMBA-treated Peyer's patches.

claims.claim: Immunostaining with the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum in Peyer's patches indicated a degree of agonist-independent phosphorylation of these sites.
claims.source: In this tissue, immunostaining with the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum indicated a degree of agonist-independent phosphorylation of these sites as this was not observed in tissue from CRE-MINUS mice, and a further increase in staining following pre-treatment with MOMBA was evident (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 5F shows basal pSer296/pSer297 staining in vehicle-treated Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice but not CRE-MINUS mice, with increased staining after MOMBA.

claims.claim: Addition of MOMBA to colonic epithelia produced a limited number of widely dispersed cells identified by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum, with minimal staining of vehicle-treated controls.
claims.source: To extend this we added vehicle or MOMBA to preparations of colonic epithelia from these mice. Subsequent immunostaining with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum identified a limited number of widely dispersed cells in MOMBA-treated tissue but minimal staining of the vehicle-treated controls (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 6A and B shows sparse pThr306/pThr310-positive cells in MOMBA-treated colonic tissue.

claims.claim: Similar experiments with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum on colonic tissue from CRE-MINUS mice failed to identify equivalent cells.
claims.source: As an additional specificity control similar experiments were performed with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum on tissue from the CRE-MINUS mice. These failed to identify equivalent cells (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 6A and B shows absence of pThr306/pThr310 staining in CRE-MINUS colonic tissue.

claims.claim: Specific agonist-mediated immuno-recognition of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA with both the anti-pThr306/pThr310 and anti-pSer296/pSer297 antisera was detected in colonic tissue, but was challenging to detect.
claims.source: Despite the limited cell expression pattern of anti-HA detected previously in colonic tissue (Bolognini et al., 2019), we were again able to specifically capture hFFAR2-DREADD-HA via HA pull-down (Figure 6C). Here, although challenging to detect, we were able to record specific agonist-mediated immuno-recognition of polypeptides of the appropriate molecular mass with both the anti-pThr306/pThr310 and anti-pSer296/pSer297 antisera that were again absent following HA pull-downs conducted in tissue from CRE-MINUS mice (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 6C shows weak but specific signals for both phospho-antisera in MOMBA-treated colonic tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice but not CRE-MINUS mice.

claims.claim: Compared to white adipose tissue or Peyer's patch immune cells, detection of pThr306/pThr310 or pSer296/pSer297 in colonic epithelial cells was modest and potentially indicated only limited phosphorylation of these sites, even after exposure to MOMBA.
claims.source: However, compared to the intensity of immunodetection of either anti-pThr306/pThr310 or anti-pSer296/pSer297 in white adipose tissue or Peyer's patch immune cells compared to the extent of anti-HA pull-down, such detection was modest and potentially indicted only limited phosphorylation of these sites in such colonic epithelial cells, even after exposure to MOMBA (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Comparison of immunoblot signal intensities across Figure 4A, Figure 5D, and Figure 6C shows weaker phosphorylation signals in colonic tissue relative to receptor expression levels.

claims.claim: Addition of C3 to Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA-expressing mice produced a marked increase in detection of hFFAR2-HA by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum compared to vehicle-treated samples.
claims.source: In immunocytochemical studies using Peyer's patches isolated from the hFFAR2-HA-expressing mice addition of C3 (10 mM, 20 min) produced a marked increase in detection of hFFAR2-HA by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum compared to vehicle-treated samples (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 8A shows increased pThr306/pThr310 staining after C3 treatment in Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice.

claims.claim: The effect of C3 on pThr306/pThr310 detection was lacking in Peyer's patches from CRE-MINUS mice.
claims.source: By contrast, such an effect of C3 was lacking in equivalent tissue isolated from equivalent CRE-MINUS comparator mice (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 8A shows no change in pThr306/pThr310 staining after C3 treatment in CRE-MINUS Peyer's patches.

claims.claim: Basal identification of anti-pSer296/pSer297 staining in Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice was significant and little altered by treatment with C3.
claims.source: Basal identification of anti-pSer296/pSer297 staining was significant (Figure 8B) and little altered by treatment with C3 (Figure 8B).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 8B shows substantial basal pSer296/pSer297 staining with minimal change after C3 treatment.

claims.claim: Basal phosphorylation of Ser296/Ser297 in Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice appeared to be specific, as it was lacking in tissue from CRE-MINUS mice.
claims.source: Such basal phosphorylation of Ser296/Ser297 did appear to be specific however, as this was lacking in tissue from the CRE-MINUS mice (Figure 8B).
claims.evidence: Immunohistochemistry data in Figure 8B shows pSer296/pSer297 staining in hFFAR2-HA mice but not CRE-MINUS mice.

claims.claim: Immunoblotting with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum showed clear phosphorylation of pThr306/pThr310 in Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice in response to C3 that increased from essentially undetectable levels in vehicle-treated cells.
claims.source: Immunoblotting such samples with the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum showed clear phosphorylation of pThr306/pThr310 in response to C3 (Figure 8C) that increased from essentially undetectable levels in samples of vehicle-treated cells (Figure 8D).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8C and quantification in Figure 8D show C3-induced pThr306/pThr310 signal in Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice.

claims.claim: The effect of C3 on pThr306/pThr310 phosphorylation in Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice was clearly produced directly at the hFFAR2-HA receptor because pre-treatment with CATPB entirely blocked the effect of C3.
claims.source: Like cells from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA-expressing Peyer's patches the effect of C3 was clearly produced directly at the hFFAR2-HA receptor because pre-treatment with CATPB entirely blocked the effect of C3 (Figure 8C and D).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8C and quantification in Figure 8D show absence of C3-induced pThr306/pThr310 signal when CATPB is present.

claims.claim: The anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum showed enhanced detection of hFFAR2-HA in Peyer's patches in response to treatment with C3 that was prevented by pre-treatment with CATPB.
claims.source: The anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum also showed enhanced detection of hFFAR2-HA in response to treatment with C3 in this setting that was also prevented by pre-treatment with CATPB (Figure 8C and D)
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8C and quantification in Figure 8D show C3-induced increase in pSer296/pSer297 signal that is blocked by CATPB.

claims.claim: The enhancement of pSer296/pSer297 detection by C3 in Peyer's patches appeared to be less pronounced than the enhancement of pThr306/pThr310 detection.
claims.source: but this appeared to be less pronounced than in the studies employing anti-pThr306/pThr310 hFFAR2.
claims.evidence: Comparison of signal changes in Figure 8C and D suggests differential magnitude of C3-induced phosphorylation at the two sites.

claims.claim: Similar levels of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA and hFFAR2-HA were observed in both white adipose tissue and colonic epithelial preparations from homozygous animals of each transgenic line.
claims.source: To assess the relative expression of hFFAR2-HA in this line compared to hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in equivalent tissues of the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA knock-in mice, we isolated both white adipocytes and colonic epithelia from homozygous animals of each line and immunoprecipitated the corresponding receptors using anti-HA. Immunoblotting of such HA immunoprecipitates showed similar levels of the corresponding receptor in each and that the molecular mass of hFFAR2-HA was equivalent to hFFAR2-DREADD-HA (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1 shows comparable expression levels and molecular weights of the two receptor constructs.

claims.claim: Immunoblots using anti-GFP confirmed similar levels of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP in vehicle and C3-treated samples.
claims.source: Parallel immunoblotting with anti-GFP confirmed the presence of similar levels of hFFAR2-eYFP both with and without treatment with C3 (Figure 7A)
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 7A shows equivalent anti-GFP signal across treatment conditions.

claims.claim: Expression of hFFAR2-eYFP was lacking if cells harbouring hFFAR2-eYFP had not been induced with doxycycline.
claims.source: and confirmed in addition that expression of the receptor construct was lacking if cells harbouring hFFAR2-eYFP had not been induced with doxycycline (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 7A shows no signal in -dox lanes.

claims.claim: C3-induced recognition of hFFAR2-eYFP by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum was lacking in the co-presence of the hFFAR2 antagonist CATPB.
claims.source: As with the effect of MOMBA on the hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP construct, in studies using the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum, C3-induced recognition of the hFFAR2-eYFP receptor was lacking in the co-presence of the hFFAR2 antagonist CATPB (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 7B shows absence of C3-induced pThr306/pThr310 signal when CATPB is present.

claims.claim: Treatment of C3-exposed samples with lambda protein phosphatase before SDS-PAGE prevented subsequent hFFAR2-eYFP identification by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum.
claims.source: In addition, treatment of C3-exposed samples to LPP before SDS-PAGE also prevented subsequent hFFAR2-eYFP identification by the anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum (Figure 7B), confirming this to reflect phosphorylation of the target.
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 7B shows loss of pThr306/pThr310 signal after LPP treatment, confirming phosphorylation-dependent detection.

claims.claim: The anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum was only able to identify hFFAR2-eYFP in immunocytochemistry after exposure to C3.
claims.source: The anti-pThr306/pThr310 antiserum was only able to identify hFFAR2-eYFP after exposure to C3 in this context (Figure 7C)
claims.evidence: Immunocytochemistry data in Figure 7C shows pThr306/pThr310 signal only in C3-treated cells.

claims.claim: The anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum identified wild-type hFFAR2-eYFP in both vehicle and C3-treated cells in immunocytochemistry.
claims.source: whereas for this construct the anti-pSer296/pSer297 antiserum identified the receptor in both vehicle and C3-treated cells (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: Immunocytochemistry data in Figure 7D shows pSer296/pSer297 signal in both vehicle and C3-treated cells.

claims.claim: Co-translational N-glycosylation, and potentially other post-translational modifications, of the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA receptor was markedly different in various tissues.
claims.source: A further interesting feature, although not inherently linked to bar-coding, is that co-translational N-glycosylation, and potentially other post-translational modifications, of the hFFAR2-DREADD-HA receptor (and probably of hFFAR2-HA) was markedly different in these various tissues.
claims.evidence: Observation based on differences in molecular weight patterns across tissues shown in immunoblots (Figures 4A, 5D, 6C).

claims.claim: The predominant form of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA in colonic epithelium migrated as a substantially larger species than that isolated from white adipocytes.
claims.source: As we were able to use the HA tag to immunoprecipitate the receptor from different tissues, SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting studies showed that the predominant form of the receptor in colonic epithelium migrated as a substantially larger species than that isolated from white adipocytes, and this was also the case when the receptor was immune-enriched from Peyer's patches and associated mesenteric lymph nodes (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Immunoblot data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2 shows different molecular weight distributions of the receptor across tissues.

claims.claim: Differences in molecular weight of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA across tissues reflect, at least in part, differential extents of N-glycosylation.
claims.source: De-glycosylation studies using an enzyme able to cleave N-linked carbohydrate confirmed these differences to reflect, at least in part, differential extents of N-glycosylation (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: De-glycosylation experiment data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2 shows altered molecular weight after N-glycosidase F treatment.

claims.claim: The same agonist-receptor pairing generates distinct phosphorylation patterns in distinct patho-physiologically relevant tissues.
claims.source: Despite this, the current studies show clear evidence of how the same ligand-GPCR pairing generates distinct phosphorylation patterns and hence different 'bar-codes' in distinct patho-physiologically relevant tissues.
claims.evidence: Summary conclusion drawn from the differential phosphorylation patterns observed across white adipose tissue, Peyer's patches, and colonic epithelium (Figures 4, 5, 6).

claims.claim: FFAR2 is expressed widely, including in white adipocytes and various immune and enteroendocrine cells.
claims.source: Free fatty acid receptor 2 (FFAR2) is activated by short-chain fatty acids and expressed widely, including in white adipocytes and various immune and enteroendocrine cells.
claims.evidence: Statement in the abstract summarizing known expression pattern.

claims.claim: In white adipose tissue, phosphorylation of residues Ser296/Ser297 was enhanced upon agonist activation.
claims.source: In white adipose tissue, phosphorylation of residues Ser296/Ser297 was enhanced upon agonist activation whilst Thr306/Thr310 did not become phosphorylated.
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by data in Figures 4A, 4B, 4D.

claims.claim: In white adipose tissue, Thr306/Thr310 did not become phosphorylated.
claims.source: In white adipose tissue, phosphorylation of residues Ser296/Ser297 was enhanced upon agonist activation whilst Thr306/Thr310 did not become phosphorylated.
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by data in Figures 4A, 4B, 4C.

claims.claim: In immune cells from Peyer's patches, Thr306/Thr310 become phosphorylated in a strictly agonist-dependent fashion.
claims.source: By contrast, in immune cells from Peyer's patches Thr306/Thr310 become phosphorylated in a strictly agonist-dependent fashion
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by data in Figures 5D, 5E, 5F.

claims.claim: In enteroendocrine cells of the colon, both Ser296/Ser297 and Thr306/Thr310 were poorly phosphorylated.
claims.source: whilst in enteroendocrine cells of the colon both Ser296/Ser297 and Thr306/Thr310 were poorly phosphorylated.
claims.evidence: Summary statement in abstract supported by data in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The concept of phosphorylation bar-coding has centred to date on the potential for different agonists to promote distinct receptor phosphorylation patterns.
claims.source: The concept of phosphorylation bar-coding has centred to date on the potential for different agonists to promote distinct receptor phosphorylation patterns.
claims.evidence: Statement summarizing the existing understanding of phosphorylation bar-coding in the field.

claims.claim: Tissue-specific phosphorylation bar-coding may underpin why a single G protein-coupled receptor can generate different functional outcomes in a tissue-specific manner.
claims.source: This may underpin why a single G protein-coupled receptor can generate different functional outcomes in a tissue-specific manner.
claims.evidence: Speculative conclusion drawn from the observed tissue-specific phosphorylation patterns.

claims.claim: GPCRs routinely are constitutively phosphorylated or become phosphorylated on serine and threonine residues following exposure to activating agonist ligands.
claims.source: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) routinely are constitutively phosphorylated or become phosphorylated on serine and threonine residues, located either within the third intracellular loop or the C-terminal tail, following exposure to activating agonist ligands (Zhang et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: General statement about GPCR phosphorylation supported by citation.

claims.claim: GPCR phosphorylation is generally accompanied by new or enhanced interactions with arrestin adapter proteins.
claims.source: This is generally accompanied by new or enhanced interactions with arrestin adapter proteins.
claims.evidence: General statement about GPCR signaling based on established knowledge.

claims.claim: Arrestin binding to GPCRs results in receptor desensitisation because the positioning of the arrestin precludes simultaneous interactions of the GPCR with a heterotrimeric G protein.
claims.source: Canonically this results in receptor desensitisation because the positioning of the arrestin precludes simultaneous interactions of the GPCR with a heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide binding (G) protein and hence 'arrests' further G protein activation (Sun and Kim, 2021).
claims.evidence: Canonical mechanism of GPCR desensitisation supported by citation.

claims.claim: Receptors exist in multiply phosphorylated states where numerous kinases are involved.
claims.source: The earliest studies on GPCR phosphorylation determined that receptors exist in multiply phosphorylated states where numerous kinases, that include members of the G protein receptor kinase (GRK) family, second messenger-regulated kinases, and even those of the casein kinase family are involved (Pitcher et al., 1998; Budd et al., 2000; Torrecilla et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Historical observation about GPCR phosphorylation supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: The pattern of receptor phosphorylation was distinct among cell types and tissues.
claims.source: Using mass spectrometry approaches and phospho-site-specific antibodies it emerged that the pattern of receptor phosphorylation was distinct among cell types and tissues (Tran et al., 2004; Nobles et al., 2011; Kaya et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Observation from previous studies supported by citations.

claims.claim: The tissue-specific signalling output of GPCRs might be determined, at least in part, by the pattern of receptor phosphorylation.
claims.source: This led to the notion that the tissue-specific signalling output of GPCRs might be determined, at least in part, by the pattern of receptor phosphorylation – a hypothesis coined the phosphorylation barcode (Nobles et al., 2011; Tobin et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Hypothesis from the field supported by citations.

claims.claim: The conformation adopted by an arrestin on interaction with the phosphorylated form of a GPCR might be affected by the pattern of receptor phosphorylation.
claims.source: This notion has recently been taken a step further with appreciation that the conformation adopted by an arrestin on interaction with the phosphorylated form of a GPCR might be affected by the pattern of receptor phosphorylation and in turn this may affect the signalling outputs mediated by arrestins (Latorraca et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Recent development in the field supported by citation.

claims.claim: Short chain fatty acids are generated in prodigious quantities by fermentation of dietary fibre by the gut microbiota.
claims.source: A number of GPCRs are able to bind and respond to short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that are generated in prodigious quantities by fermentation of dietary fibre by the gut microbiota (Xie et al., 2023; Tan et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: Established biological fact supported by citations.

claims.claim: FFAR2 is the most studied and best characterised GPCR that responds to short chain fatty acids.
claims.source: The most studied and best characterised of these is FFAR2 (also designated GPR43) (Bolognini et al., 2016b; Stoddart et al., 2008; Ikeda et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: Statement about the state of the field supported by citations.

claims.claim: FFAR2 is expressed by a range of immune cells, adipocytes, enteroendocrine, and pancreatic cells.
claims.source: This receptor is expressed widely, including by a range of immune cells, adipocytes, enteroendocrine, and pancreatic cells (Bolognini et al., 2016b; Stoddart et al., 2008; Ikeda et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: Known expression pattern supported by citations.

claims.claim: FFAR2 is able to couple to a range of different heterotrimeric G proteins from each of the Gi, Gq, and G12/G13 families when expressed in simple heterologous cell lines.
claims.source: In addition to being widely expressed FFAR2 is, at least when expressed in simple heterologous cell lines, able to couple to a range of different heterotrimeric G proteins from each of the Gi, Gq, and G12/G13 families (Brown et al., 2003; Bolognini et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Known signaling properties supported by citations.

claims.claim: In white adipocytes, stimulation of FFAR2 is anti-lipolytic, an effect mediated via pertussis toxin-sensitive Gi proteins and reduction in cellular cAMP levels.
claims.source: For example, in white adipocytes stimulation of FFAR2 is clearly anti-lipolytic, an effect mediated via pertussis toxin-sensitive Gi proteins and reduction in cellular cAMP levels (Bolognini et al., 2016a)
claims.evidence: Known functional effect in specific cell type supported by citation.

claims.claim: In GLP-1-positive enteroendocrine cells, activation of FFAR2 promotes release of GLP-1 in a Ca2+ and Gq-mediated manner.
claims.source: whilst in GLP-1-positive enteroendocrine cells activation of FFAR2 promotes release of this incretin hormone in a Ca2+ and Gq-mediated manner (Bolognini et al., 2016a).
claims.evidence: Known functional effect in specific cell type supported by citation.

claims.claim: The pharmacology of the various GPCRs that respond to SCFAs is very limited.
claims.source: A challenge in studying the molecular basis of effects of SCFAs in native cells and tissues is that the pharmacology of the various GPCRs that respond to these ligands is very limited (Milligan et al., 2017a; Milligan et al., 2017b)
claims.evidence: Known limitation in the field supported by citations.

claims.claim: There is a particular dearth of antagonist ligands for anything other than the human ortholog of FFAR2.
claims.source: and there is a particular dearth of antagonist ligands for anything other than the human ortholog of FFAR2 (Milligan et al., 2017a; Milligan et al., 2017b).
claims.evidence: Known limitation in the field supported by citations.

claims.claim: Designer receptor exclusively activated by designer drug (DREADD) forms of GPCRs contain mutations that eliminate binding and responsiveness to endogenously generated orthosteric agonists whilst allowing binding and activation by defined, non-endogenously produced ligands.
claims.source: Designer receptor exclusively activated by designer drug (DREADD) forms of GPCRs contain mutations that eliminate binding and responsiveness to endogenously generated orthosteric agonists whilst, in parallel, allowing binding and activation by defined, but non-endogenously produced, ligands that do not activate the wild-type form of the receptor (Wang et al., 2021; Bradley et al., 2018; Shchepinova et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Definition and properties of DREADDs supported by citations.

claims.claim: The hFFAR2-DREADD variant differs from wild-type receptor only in two amino acids of the orthosteric ligand binding pocket (Cys141Gly, His242Gln).
claims.source: Moreover, as the DREADD variant differs from wild-type receptor only in two amino acids of the orthosteric ligand binding pocket, and the intracellular sections of the two forms are identical (Bolognini et al., 2019)
claims.evidence: Structural information about the DREADD variant shown in Figure 2A and supported by citation.

claims.claim: The intracellular sections of hFFAR2-DREADD and wild-type hFFAR2 are identical.
claims.source: Moreover, as the DREADD variant differs from wild-type receptor only in two amino acids of the orthosteric ligand binding pocket, and the intracellular sections of the two forms are identical (Bolognini et al., 2019)
claims.evidence: Structural information supported by citation.

results.result: Mass spectrometry identified constitutive phosphorylation of Ser297 and agonist-induced phosphorylation of Ser296/297 in hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP expressed in Flp-In T-REx 293 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1 and C2 are directly supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1, which provides direct molecular evidence of phosphorylation at these specific residues under basal and agonist-stimulated conditions. The fragmentation tables confirm the identification of phosphorylated peptides.

results.result: The pSer296/pSer297 antiserum specifically detects hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP in both basal and agonist-stimulated conditions, with increased signal after MOMBA treatment, and fails to detect the Ser296Ala/Ser297Ala variant.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C5 are well-supported by immunoblot data in Figure 2B showing basal detection, MOMBA-enhanced signal, and absence of signal in the PD1 mutant. This demonstrates both the sensitivity and specificity of the antiserum for phosphorylated Ser296/297.

results.result: The pThr306/pThr310 antiserum shows minimal basal detection but strong agonist-dependent identification of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP, and fails to detect the Thr306Ala/Thr310Ala variant.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C8 are supported by immunoblot data in Figure 2B demonstrating agonist-dependent detection and specificity confirmed by absence of signal in the PD2 mutant. This establishes the antiserum as a specific tool for detecting phosphorylated Thr306/310.

results.result: MOMBA promotes arrestin-3 recruitment to hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP in a concentration-dependent manner (pEC50=4.62±0.13 M), with reduced maximal responses in phospho-deficient variants except PD2, and dramatically reduced recruitment (~21% of wild-type) in the PD1-4 variant lacking all C-terminal phospho-acceptor sites.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C11 are supported by BRET data in Figure 2C showing concentration-response curves and quantified maximal responses. The data demonstrate that C-terminal phosphorylation contributes to arrestin-3 recruitment, though no single site is solely responsible.

results.result: GRK2/3 inhibition with compound 101 greatly reduces MOMBA-induced arrestin-3 recruitment but does not substantially reduce phosphorylation at Ser296/297 or Thr306/310, indicating these sites are not controlled by GRK2/3 and are insufficient alone to define arrestin-3 interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C15 are supported by BRET data (Figure 2D) and immunoblot data (Figure 2E). The differential effects of compound 101 on arrestin recruitment versus phosphorylation at these specific sites provide strong evidence that GRK2/3 phosphorylates other sites critical for arrestin binding.

results.result: Sorbic acid, a second hFFAR2-DREADD agonist, recapitulates MOMBA's effects on Ser296/297 and Thr306/310 phosphorylation, while propionic acid (C3), which does not activate hFFAR2-DREADD, fails to modulate phosphorylation at either site.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C19 are supported by immunoblot data in Figure 3A demonstrating agonist specificity. The lack of effect with C3 provides important negative control evidence confirming that the observed phosphorylation is receptor-mediated and specific to hFFAR2-DREADD agonists.

results.result: The inverse agonist CATPB prevents MOMBA-induced phosphorylation at both Ser296/297 and Thr306/310, and reduces basal pSer296/pSer297 detection, suggesting that basal phosphorylation reflects constitutive receptor activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C22 are supported by immunoblot data in Figure 3B. The ability of the inverse agonist to reduce basal phosphorylation provides evidence for constitutive activity, though claim C22 is somewhat inferential based on the known properties of CATPB.

results.result: Lambda protein phosphatase (LPP) treatment eliminates detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by both phospho-specific antisera, confirming they detect phosphorylated forms of the receptor.
results.evaluation: Claim C23 is directly supported by immunoblot data in Figure 3B showing loss of signal after LPP treatment. This is a critical control demonstrating that the antisera specifically recognize phosphorylated epitopes.

results.result: Immunocytochemistry studies confirm agonist-dependent detection of hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP by both phospho-specific antisera, with CATPB preventing MOMBA-induced signals.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C27 are supported by immunocytochemistry data in Figures 3C and 3D. These studies extend the immunoblot findings to intact cells and provide spatial information about receptor phosphorylation.

results.result: In white adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice, the receptor is detected as ~45 kDa and ~40 kDa species, with basal pSer296/pSer297 phosphorylation that is enhanced by MOMBA, while Thr306/310 are not phosphorylated either basally or after agonist treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C33 are supported by immunoblot data in Figures 4A and 4B showing tissue-specific phosphorylation patterns. The absence of pThr306/310 signal in white adipose tissue represents a key finding demonstrating tissue-specific phosphorylation bar-coding.

results.result: Immunohistochemistry of white adipose tissue confirms agonist-enhanced pSer296/pSer297 staining and absence of pThr306/310 staining, with co-localization with perilipin-1 confirming receptor presence on adipocytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C38 are supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figures 4C-F. The co-localization studies provide important validation that the phosphorylated receptor is present on adipocytes, and the CRE-MINUS controls confirm specificity.

results.result: hFFAR2-DREADD-HA is extensively expressed in Peyer's patches, with many positive cells corresponding to dendritic cells, monocytes, macrophages (CD11c+), and type-III innate lymphoid cells (RORγt+).
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C41 are supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figures 5A-C showing receptor expression and co-localization with cell-type markers. The identification of specific immune cell populations expressing the receptor is well-documented.

results.result: In Peyer's patches, hFFAR2-DREADD-HA shows a more diffuse molecular weight pattern than in white adipose tissue, and becomes phosphorylated on Thr306/310 in a strictly MOMBA-dependent manner that is blocked by CATPB, while pSer296/297 shows low basal levels that are increased by MOMBA.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C46 are supported by immunoblot data in Figures 5D and 5E. The tissue-specific phosphorylation of Thr306/310 in Peyer's patches but not white adipose tissue is a central finding demonstrating differential phosphorylation bar-coding.

results.result: Immunohistochemistry of Peyer's patches confirms agonist-dependent pThr306/310 staining and shows agonist-independent pSer296/297 phosphorylation that is further enhanced by MOMBA.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C48 are supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 5F with appropriate CRE-MINUS controls. The spatial distribution of phosphorylated receptors within Peyer's patches is well-documented.

results.result: In colonic epithelium, MOMBA treatment produces limited pThr306/310-positive cells, and immunoblot detection of both pThr306/310 and pSer296/297 is modest compared to white adipose tissue or Peyer's patches, indicating limited phosphorylation at these sites even after agonist exposure.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C52 are supported by immunohistochemistry (Figures 6A-B) and immunoblot data (Figure 6C). The weak signals relative to receptor expression levels suggest tissue-specific differences in phosphorylation efficiency or kinase expression, representing a third distinct phosphorylation pattern.

results.result: In Peyer's patches from wild-type hFFAR2-HA mice, C3 (a natural SCFA agonist) produces marked agonist-dependent phosphorylation of Thr306/310 that is blocked by CATPB, while pSer296/297 shows significant basal phosphorylation with modest C3-induced enhancement.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C60 are supported by immunohistochemistry (Figures 8A-B) and immunoblot data (Figures 8C-D) from the wild-type hFFAR2-HA mouse line. These results demonstrate that the phosphorylation patterns observed with the DREADD receptor are recapitulated with the wild-type receptor and its natural agonists.

results.result: Similar expression levels and molecular weights of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA and hFFAR2-HA were observed in white adipose tissue and colonic epithelium from the two transgenic mouse lines.
results.evaluation: Claim C61 is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1. This comparison validates that the two mouse lines express comparable levels of receptor, supporting the validity of comparisons between DREADD and wild-type receptor studies.

results.result: In Flp-In T-REx 293 cells expressing wild-type hFFAR2-eYFP, C3 induces phosphorylation detected by both antisera, with pThr306/310 detection being strictly agonist-dependent and blocked by CATPB or LPP treatment, while pSer296/297 shows both basal and C3-enhanced detection.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C67 are supported by immunoblot (Figures 7A-B) and immunocytochemistry data (Figures 7C-D). These studies demonstrate that wild-type hFFAR2 shows similar phosphorylation patterns to the DREADD variant when activated by natural agonists.

results.result: The hFFAR2-DREADD-HA receptor shows markedly different N-glycosylation patterns across tissues, with colonic epithelium and Peyer's patches showing larger molecular weight species than white adipose tissue, as confirmed by de-glycosylation studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C70 are supported by immunoblot data comparing tissues (Figures 4A, 5D, 6C) and de-glycosylation experiments (Figure 8—figure supplement 2). This represents an important observation about tissue-specific post-translational modifications beyond phosphorylation.

results.result: The same agonist-receptor pairing generates distinct tissue-specific phosphorylation bar-codes: in white adipose tissue, Ser296/297 phosphorylation is enhanced by agonist while Thr306/310 are not phosphorylated; in Peyer's patches immune cells, Thr306/310 become phosphorylated in an agonist-dependent manner; and in colonic enteroendocrine cells, both sites show poor phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C71 and C73-C76 represent the central conclusion of the manuscript, supported by the collective data from Figures 4-6 and 8. The tissue-specific phosphorylation patterns are well-documented across multiple experimental approaches (immunoblot, immunohistochemistry) and with appropriate controls.

results.result: Tissue-specific phosphorylation bar-coding may underpin why a single GPCR can generate different functional outcomes in different tissues.
results.evaluation: Claim C78 is speculative and represents a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated result. While the manuscript clearly shows tissue-specific phosphorylation patterns, the functional consequences of these different patterns are not directly tested. Additional experiments linking specific phosphorylation patterns to distinct functional outcomes would be needed to support this claim.

results.result: Background and context claims about GPCR phosphorylation, FFAR2 expression and function, and DREADD technology.
results.evaluation: Claims C28 and C72-C96 represent established knowledge from the literature, supported by appropriate citations. These provide necessary context for the experimental work but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: Mass spectrometry identified constitutive phosphorylation at Ser297 and agonist-induced phosphorylation at Ser296/297 in hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP expressed in Flp-In T-REx 293 cells (Figure 1).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 4 explicitly challenges the mass spectrometry analysis, stating 'The mass spectrometry analysis is not convincing because the method is not quantitative (no SILAC, TMT, internal standards etc)' and notes 'there is no data testing the abundance of these so the differences claimed between cell treatment conditions are not established.' This directly questions the validity of the MS-based phosphorylation site identification.

results.result: The pSer296/pSer297 antiserum specifically detects hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP in vehicle-treated cells with increased intensity after MOMBA treatment, and fails to detect the Ser296Ala/Ser297Ala variant (PD1) (Figure 2B).
results.evaluation: Reviewers 1, 2, and 3 all affirm the antibody characterization as convincing. Reviewer 2 states 'Technical tour de force, rigorous experimental approaches' and Reviewer 3 notes 'strengths include the initial experimental controls employed in characterizing their ever-important antisera...showing strong agonist-dependent and phosphosite-dependent recognition.' Reviewer 4 acknowledges 'the antibody characterization is convincing.'

results.result: The pThr306/pThr310 antiserum shows minimal detection in vehicle-treated cells, strong agonist-dependent detection after MOMBA treatment, and fails to detect the Thr306Ala/Thr310Ala variant (PD2) (Figure 2B).
results.evaluation: Reviewers consistently affirm the antibody validation. Reviewer 3 specifically notes the antisera 'give clear indications of differences across variables in immunoblots' and that the authors 'substantiate the role of the antiserum in recognizing their intended motifs.' The phosphosite-dependent recognition through PD variant controls is highlighted as a strength.

results.result: MOMBA promotes arrestin-3 recruitment to hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP in a concentration-dependent manner (pEC50=4.62±0.13 M), with reduced maximal effects for phospho-deficient variants except PD2, and dramatically reduced recruitment (20.8±2.3% of wild-type) for the PD1-4 variant lacking all C-terminal phospho-acceptor sites (Figure 2C).
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these arrestin recruitment data. Reviewer 3 notes the experimental controls are convincing and the immunoblots 'give clear indications of differences across variables.' The BRET-based functional data complement the antibody characterization and are accepted as part of the rigorous validation.

results.result: The GRK2/GRK3 inhibitor compound 101 greatly reduced MOMBA-induced arrestin-3 recruitment (Figure 2D) but did not substantially reduce phosphorylation detected by either pThr306/pThr310 or pSer296/pSer297 antisera (Figure 2E), suggesting these sites are not controlled by GRK2/3 and are not sufficient alone to define arrestin-3 interactions.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 4 questions the indirect approach, stating 'Compound 101 is shown in Figure 2 to block barrestin recruitment. I agree this suggests phosphorylation mediated by GRK2/3 but this is not tested. The new antibodies should be good for this so I don't understand why the indirect approach.' This indicates the mechanistic conclusion about GRK2/3 independence requires more direct testing.

results.result: Sorbic acid recapitulated MOMBA's effects on phosphorylation of Ser296/Ser297 and Thr306/Thr310, while propionic acid (C3), which does not activate hFFAR2-DREADD, failed to modulate phosphorylation at either site (Figure 3A).
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these ligand selectivity data. Reviewer 2 and 3 emphasize the rigorous use of both wild-type and DREADD versions to ensure ligand- and receptor-dependent specificity. The differential effects of DREADD-selective vs. endogenous agonists support the specificity of the antisera.

results.result: The inverse agonist CATPB prevented MOMBA-induced phosphorylation at both sites and reduced basal pSer296/pSer297 detection (Figure 3B), suggesting basal phosphorylation reflects constitutive receptor activity. Lambda protein phosphatase (LPP) treatment eliminated both agonist-induced and basal phosphorylation signals (Figure 3B).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 specifically highlights 'the addition of GRK inhibitors and eventually an antagonist and phosphatase treatment' as strengths that 'substantiate the role of the antiserum in recognizing their intended motifs.' These pharmacological and enzymatic controls are viewed as convincing validation.

results.result: In immunocytochemistry, the pThr306/pThr310 antiserum detected hFFAR2-DREADD-eYFP only after MOMBA treatment (Figure 3C), while pSer296/pSer297 detection was almost entirely MOMBA-dependent (Figure 3D), with both effects prevented by CATPB.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes that 'while the immunocytochemical studies are qualitative and at times not visually significantly different across all variables, they are in large part congruent with the results of the immunoblots and provide secondary supporting evidence for the author's major claims.' The consistency with immunoblot data supports these findings despite some visual limitations.

results.result: In white adipose tissue from hFFAR2-DREADD-HA mice, the pSer296/pSer297 antiserum detected basal phosphorylation that increased with MOMBA treatment (Figures 4A, 4B), while pThr306/pThr310 showed no detection in either basal or MOMBA-treated conditions (Figures 4A, 4B, 4C), indicating Thr306/Thr310 do not become phosphorylated in this tissue.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 raises concerns about 'the presence of background pThr306/pThr310, like in Figures 4C' noting 'while the immunoblot shows a complete absence of pThr306/pThr310, Figure 4C's immuno image does not.' Reviewer 4 questions 'How do the authors know that low P at 306/7 in white fat is not a result of dephosphorylation during sample preparation?' and asks 'If these sites are GRK2/3 dependent...then does adipose tissue lack this GRK?' These concerns indicate uncertainty about the tissue-specific absence of Thr306/310 phosphorylation.

results.result: Immunohistochemistry of white adipose tissue showed basal pSer296/pSer297 staining that markedly increased after MOMBA treatment (Figure 4D), with co-localization with perilipin-1 confirming presence on adipocytes (Figure 4F).
results.evaluation: Despite some concerns about background in immunocytochemistry, Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'the indication of differences in phosphorylation states between tissues is still evident across the experiments' and the paper is 'overall strongly well-researched, well-controlled.' The perilipin-1 co-localization provides additional specificity.

results.result: In Peyer's patches, hFFAR2-DREADD-HA showed extensive expression (Figure 5A) with many cells corresponding to dendritic cells, monocytes, and/or macrophages (CD11c-positive, Figure 5B) and type-III innate lymphoid cells (RORγt-positive, Figure 5C).
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the cell-type identification data. The co-staining with established markers (CD11c, RORγt) and consistency with previous mRNA expression data provide convincing evidence for the cellular localization.

results.result: In Peyer's patches, hFFAR2-DREADD-HA became phosphorylated at Thr306/Thr310 in a strictly MOMBA-dependent manner with no basal phosphorylation (Figures 5D, 5E, 5F), while pSer296/pSer297 showed low basal levels that increased markedly with MOMBA (Figures 5D, 5E, 5F), with both effects blocked by CATPB.
results.evaluation: Reviewers 1, 2, and 3 affirm the tissue-specific phosphorylation patterns. Reviewer 3 states 'the indication of differences in phosphorylation states between tissues is still evident across the experiments' and 'Providing direct evidence for the tissue-based branch of the barcode hypothesis is both novel and significant for the field.' The contrast with white adipose tissue is a key finding.

results.result: In colonic epithelium, MOMBA treatment produced sparse pThr306/pThr310-positive cells (Figures 6A, 6B), and immunoprecipitation detected weak but specific agonist-mediated signals for both phospho-antisera (Figure 6C), indicating only limited phosphorylation compared to white adipose tissue or Peyer's patches.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes 'a similar presence of pThr306/pThr310 is seen in the vehicle image, which is not strikingly over-shown by the MOMBA-treated image' in Figure 6A and B, and suggests 'the aforementioned detection in the immunocytochemical vehicle image could support differential basal phosphorylation in the enteroendocrine cells.' The weak signals and potential background complicate interpretation of the colonic data.

results.result: In Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice, the endogenous agonist C3 produced marked increases in pThr306/pThr310 detection from essentially undetectable basal levels (Figures 8A, 8C, 8D), with effects blocked by CATPB, confirming direct receptor-mediated phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the wild-type receptor data with endogenous agonist. Reviewer 2 emphasizes the 'rigorous experimental approaches taking advantage of wt and DREADD versions of FFA2 to make sure that ligand-and receptor-dependent phosphorylations are indeed specific to FFA2.' The consistency between DREADD and wild-type receptor responses strengthens the findings.

results.result: In Peyer's patches from hFFAR2-HA mice, basal pSer296/pSer297 staining was significant and specific (absent in CRE-MINUS mice) but showed less pronounced enhancement by C3 compared to pThr306/pThr310 (Figures 8B, 8C, 8D).
results.evaluation: The differential magnitude of C3 effects on the two phosphorylation sites is consistent with the DREADD data and not challenged by reviewers. The CRE-MINUS control provides specificity confirmation.

results.result: In Flp-In T-REx 293 cells expressing wild-type hFFAR2-eYFP, C3 induced pThr306/pThr310 phosphorylation in an agonist-dependent manner (blocked by CATPB and eliminated by LPP treatment, Figures 7A, 7B, 7C), while pSer296/pSer297 was detected in both vehicle and C3-treated cells (Figure 7D).
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the wild-type receptor validation in cell culture. The consistency with DREADD data and inclusion of pharmacological and enzymatic controls support these findings as part of the rigorous validation approach praised by reviewers.

results.result: N-glycosylation and other post-translational modifications of hFFAR2-DREADD-HA differed markedly across tissues, with colonic epithelium and Peyer's patches showing substantially larger molecular weight species than white adipocytes (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), confirmed by de-glycosylation studies.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the glycosylation data. This observation is presented as an additional finding ('not inherently linked to bar-coding') and the de-glycosylation experiments provide direct biochemical evidence.

results.result: The same agonist-receptor pairing generates distinct tissue-specific phosphorylation 'bar-codes': in white adipose tissue, Ser296/Ser297 phosphorylation is enhanced while Thr306/Thr310 remain unphosphorylated; in Peyer's patches immune cells, Thr306/Thr310 become phosphorylated in a strictly agonist-dependent manner; and in colonic enteroendocrine cells, both sites show poor phosphorylation. This tissue-specific phosphorylation bar-coding may underpin tissue-specific functional outcomes.
results.evaluation: While Reviewers 1, 2, and 3 affirm the overall finding of tissue-specific phosphorylation patterns as novel and significant, Reviewer 4's concerns about the mass spectrometry quantification, potential dephosphorylation artifacts in adipose tissue, and background signals in immunocytochemistry introduce uncertainty about the robustness of the tissue-specific differences. Reviewer 3 notes 'the indication of differences in phosphorylation states between tissues is still evident' but also points out visual inconsistencies and suggests 'normalized quantification of these images...may help in clearing up these hard-to-compare visual images.'

comparisons.comparison: Both address mass spectrometry identification of phosphorylation sites C1 and C2. OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with direct molecular evidence, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 4's concerns about lack of quantitative MS methods (no SILAC, TMT, internal standards) and insufficient testing of phosphopeptide abundance differences between conditions.

Both evaluate antibody characterization for pSer296/297 (C3-C5). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers (1-4) all affirming the antibody validation as convincing and rigorous, highlighting the use of mutant controls and agonist-dependent detection.

Both assess antibody characterization for pThr306/310 (C6-C8). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers emphasizing the phosphosite-dependent recognition through PD variant controls and clear agonist-dependent signals as key strengths.

Both evaluate arrestin-3 recruitment data (C9-C11). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the BRET data as part of rigorous validation complementing the antibody characterization, with no challenges raised.

Both address GRK2/3 independence of phosphorylation sites (C12-C15). OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED based on compound 101 effects, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 4 questions the indirect approach, noting the new antibodies should enable direct testing rather than relying on arrestin recruitment inhibition.

Both evaluate agonist specificity (C16-C19). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers emphasize the rigorous use of both wild-type and DREADD versions to ensure ligand- and receptor-dependent specificity, with differential effects providing strong validation.

Both address inverse agonist and phosphatase treatment (C20-C23). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED though notes C22 is somewhat inferential, while peer reviewers rate them SUPPORTED, specifically highlighting pharmacological and enzymatic controls as convincing validation strengths.

OpenEval evaluates phosphatase treatment specificity (C23) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address this as part of broader pharmacological controls (C20-C23) and find it SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 highlighting phosphatase treatment as substantiating the antisera specificity.

Both evaluate immunocytochemistry validation in cells (C24-C27). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note the immunocytochemistry is qualitative and not always visually striking but is congruent with immunoblot data and provides secondary supporting evidence.

Both address tissue-specific phosphorylation in white adipose tissue (C29-C33). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate them UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 3 notes discrepancies between immunoblot (no signal) and immunocytochemistry (background present), and Reviewer 4 questions whether low phosphorylation could be a dephosphorylation artifact or reflect GRK2/3 absence.

Both evaluate adipocyte localization and perilipin-1 co-staining (C34-C38). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers also rate them SUPPORTED despite some background concerns. Reviewer 3 acknowledges tissue-specific phosphorylation differences are still evident and the work is well-controlled overall.

OpenEval addresses broader adipose tissue claims (C34-C38) including perilipin co-localization, while peer R9 focuses on the absence of pThr306/310 signal (C30-C33). Both overlap on tissue-specific patterns but peer reviewers express more uncertainty about the robustness of the absence claim.

Both evaluate immune cell localization in Peyer's patches (C39-C41). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these claims are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not challenge the cell-type identification data, with co-staining using established markers providing convincing evidence.
